protagonist.note: Internal working name only. It must NEVER be written, lettered or monogrammed anywhere inside an illustration.
protagonist.identity: One single recurring boy, six years old, appearing in all 101 illustrations.
protagonist.apparent_age: 6 years old — a school-age child, clearly past toddlerhood and clearly far from adolescence
age_guardrails: NOT a toddler: no chubby baby cheeks, no oversized head-to-body ratio, no diaper-era proportions
NOT a teenager: no long limbs, no slim adolescent face, no styled or long hair, no adult jawline
Head is large and rounded but the body already reads as a school child: roughly 1 : 4.5 head-to-body

face.shape: soft rounded oval, gently wider at the cheeks, small softly rounded chin
face.eyes: large, round, wide-set; a bold circular outline filled solid black except for one small round white highlight in the upper-left of each pupil; a fine upper lash line; no eyelashes fanning out, no eyeliner
face.eyebrows: two short, slightly curved tapered strokes set well above the eyes, thin relative to the contour line
face.nose: very small, a single short rounded stroke or tiny soft button — never nostrils, never a realistic bridge
face.mouth: wide cheerful open smile showing a clean white mouth interior; upper teeth may be suggested by a simple curved line; tongue only when the expression calls for it
face.cheeks: two small oval blush marks, drawn as thin open outlines (never filled, never hatched), one on each cheek
face.ears: small, simple rounded ears with a single interior curve, visible at the sides of the head

hair.colour_treatment: outline only — never filled black, never shaded; the hair must be a closed white area a child can colour
hair.style: short boyish cut with a tousled, softly spiky fringe; several pointed tufts along the top and hairline
hair.internal_detail: 3–6 long flowing strand lines drawn with the thinner interior line weight to suggest direction and volume
hair.consistency_rule: the silhouette of the fringe and the tufted crown must stay recognisably the same in every illustration, regardless of pose or angle

body.proportions: head-to-body about 1 : 4.5; sturdy little torso, short rounded limbs, small hands and feet
body.hands: simple rounded mitten-style hands with FIVE clearly separated fingers, drawn cleanly and never merged, never extra, never missing
body.build: healthy, average; not thin, not heavy

wardrobe.signature: The collection's signature garment: a short-sleeved t-shirt carrying ONE single outlined five-point star emblem centred on the chest. The star is a plain outline shape — it is never a letter, number, word or logo.
wardrobe.default_outfit: short-sleeved star t-shirt, knee-length shorts with a simple rolled cuff, short socks, and chunky rounded sneakers with two or three simple strap or lace lines
wardrobe.variation_rule: Clothing may and should change to suit the activity — pyjamas for sleep, a coat and scarf for cold weather, a swimsuit for water, a sports kit for games, an apron for cooking. Whenever the activity plausibly allows it, keep the star t-shirt, because it is the strongest recognition cue in the collection.
wardrobe.forbidden_on_clothing: no text, no letters, no numbers, no brand marks, no printed slogans, no jersey numbers

protagonist.expression_range: cheerful and warm by default: bright open smile, raised eyebrows, lively eyes. Gentle variation is welcome and expected — proud, curious, concentrating, surprised, delighted, calm, thoughtful, kind. Distress is only ever mild and always resolved inside the same picture (e.g. a small frown while breathing deeply to calm down). Never frightened, never crying hard, never angry at the reader.

supporting_cast.rule: When the manuscript entry involves other people — classmates, friends, teammates, a teacher, a parent, a sibling, a new child at school — draw them, and make them visibly DIFFERENT PEOPLE.
distinctness_requirements: vary hairstyle and hair length clearly (curly, braided, straight, buzzed, bunches, afro, bob)
vary face shape, eye size and smile
vary height and build noticeably — children of the same age differ
vary clothing shape and colour-areas; NO other child ever wears the star t-shirt
vary pose and what each child is doing
include girls and boys, and a natural mix of skin tones expressed ONLY through line work (never shading or fill) so every child stays fully colourable
supporting_cast.anti_clone_rule: Never duplicate the protagonist's face, hair or outfit on another character. No twins, no mirrored copies, no repeated identical children in a crowd.
supporting_cast.adults: Adults are drawn taller with adult proportions (head-to-body about 1 : 6), simple friendly faces, calm supportive body language. They are clearly grown-ups, never large children.
supporting_cast.group_size: Keep groups readable: normally 1–3 additional characters, at most 4, so every shape stays large enough to colour.

style.medium: professional children's coloring-book line art, pure black ink on pure white

line_weight.primary_contour: thick, smooth, confident, perfectly even — the outer silhouette of every figure and major object
line_weight.interior_detail: noticeably thinner than the contour — folds, strands, small features
line_weight.rule: two clear weights only; no tapering calligraphic strokes, no sketchy multi-pass lines

fill_and_shading.allowed: closed white areas, bounded by line only
fill_and_shading.forbidden: grey tones, gradients, cross-hatching, stippling for shade, drop shadows, filled black regions larger than an eye pupil, dark backgrounds

style.colourability: Every enclosed area must be large enough for a 6-year-old to fill with a crayon. Detail is deliberately limited; no fine texture, no micro-patterning.

background.treatment: light, airy and decorative, never crowded
background.signature_motifs: scattered five-point star outlines of assorted sizes, small open circles, and four-point sparkle glints — the collection's constant background confetti
background.environment: a few large, simple, relevant props or scenery shapes that make the concept legible (tree, slide, swing, bed, table, bookshelf silhouette, bushes, clouds, a simple ground line)
background.ink_budget: background must stay well inside the measured envelope: total page ink coverage 4–9%, white 90–95%

style.concept_inset: When an idea needs a second visual beat (a growing bone, a new tooth, a heartbeat), draw it as a plain circular vignette floating in the background with simple radiating glint lines — exactly as the previous book does. The vignette contains a drawing only, never a caption.

composition.subject_scale: the protagonist is the unmistakable focal point, filling a generous share of the frame
composition.framing_variety: deliberately mix full-body shots, three-quarter shots, medium shots, close-ups, low and high angles, and active diagonal action poses across the 101 pages
composition.pose_variety: no two consecutive illustrations repeat the same stance; running, reaching, crouching, jumping, sitting, balancing, leaning, kneeling, lying down
composition.safe_area: all meaningful line work stays inside the printable safe area — nothing important within 0.25in of any edge

absolute_prohibitions.written_language: The illustrations must contain NO written language of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, digits, captions, labels, signs, titles, speech bubbles with text, watermarks, signatures, logos, pseudo-text or AI gibberish typography.
absolute_prohibitions.blank_surface_rule: Any surface that would normally carry writing must be redrawn BLANK or replaced with purely non-linguistic symbols: a classroom board shows a simple drawing or is empty; a book shows blank pages or a plain picture; a clock shows tick marks and hands but no numerals; a ruler or height chart shows tick marks only; a calendar shows an empty grid; a screen is blank or shows a simple shape; a shop sign is an empty plaque or a pictogram; a scoreboard shows dots.
absolute_prohibitions.rendering: no colour, no greyscale shading, no gradients, no photorealism, no 3D rendering, no painterly texture, no heavy hatching
absolute_prohibitions.anatomy: no malformed or extra or missing fingers, no extra or duplicated limbs, no distorted or merged faces, no fused bodies, no floating detached parts
absolute_prohibitions.cropping: never crop the head; never crop hands or feet when a full-body composition is intended
absolute_prohibitions.content: nothing frightening, unsafe or age-inappropriate; no injuries; no blood; helmets shown where a real child would wear one

per_page_variation_checklist: Has the framing changed from the previous page?
Has the pose changed from the previous page?
Is the setting varied across the section (home, school, park, playground, street, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, sports ground)?
Does the scene show the manuscript's IDEA, not just a decorative child?
Is every writing surface blank or symbolic?
Is the protagonist recognisably the same 6-year-old boy?
Are any additional characters clearly distinct individuals?
